description: We are ChronoNova, a group of passionate innovators combining computer science, design, and interactive media. Our shared interest in space exploration and UI/UX brought us together for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our goal is to create a visual, interactive platform that brings forgotten space missions back to life. We believe space history should be accessible, engaging, and inspiring for everyone around the world.
summary: Legacy of Space is an educational NASA Space Apps Challenge project designed to introduce students and young space enthusiasts to the history of space exploration hardware. The website catalogs notable spacecraft, rovers, landers, helicopters, and probes across three main regions: the Moon, Mars, and deep space. Each mission entry highlights key details such as operational years, landing locations or destinations, current status, and scientific achievements. Built using official NASA scientific sources, the platform emphasizes that these inactive or active machines are not just discarded equipment, but enduring symbols of human curiosity, scientific discovery, and engineering.
details:
What It Does & How It Works
Legacy of Space is an interactive educational web platform that catalogs the spacecraft, rovers, landers, helicopters, and probes humanity has sent across the Moon, Mars, and deep space. Users can browse missions organized by celestial destination and explore structured mission cards featuring operational timelines, landing sites or destinations, current mission status, key scientific breakthroughs, and expandable details sourced directly from official NASA archives.

Benefits & Intended Impact
Space exploration history is often scattered across dense technical archives that can feel overwhelming for younger audiences. Legacy of Space makes this information accessible, structured, and engaging for students and young space enthusiasts. Our goal is to inspire the next generation of explorers by showing that spacecraft left behind on other worlds—or still traveling through deep space—are not just discarded hardware, but enduring milestones of human curiosity, engineering, and scientific discovery.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Web Development & Data: Built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for a clean, responsive user interface, with structured JSON files to store and dynamically render mission details.
  • Development & Deployment: Developed in Visual Studio Code (VS Code) and deployed via Cloudflare Pages for fast, reliable global access.
  • Research & Data: Official NASA portals, including NASA Science, NASA Solar System Exploration, and NASA Mars Exploration archives.

Creativity & Design Considerations
Rather than treating historical missions as static encyclopedia entries, we framed each piece of space hardware around its ongoing story and legacy. When designing the platform, our team focused on three key factors:

  • Accessibility for Young Learners: Using clear, jargon-free summaries, visual categorization by destination, and scannable status badges so students can grasp complex missions quickly.
  • Scientific Accuracy: Cross-referencing every mission detail against authoritative NASA resources and linking users directly to original sources for deeper learning.
  • Intuitive User Experience: Organizing missions geographically—from the Moon to Mars to interstellar space—so visitors experience a natural sense of scale and progression as they explore.
